name: Kailash Satyarthi
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan (Save Childhood Movement) in 1980 at age 26, India's first grassroots movement against child labor, trafficking, and slavery, after giving up his career as an electrical engineer.
early_history_summary: Satyarthi grew up in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, disturbed by child labor from age five. He earned B.E. and M.E. degrees in electrical engineering and worked briefly as a college lecturer before abandoning his career in 1980 to found Bachpan Bachao Andolan, conducting the first rescue of a bonded child laborer that same year.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Vidisha; father Ramprasad Sharma was a retired police head constable and mother Chironjibai was a housewife with little formal education but high moral standards.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct activism or social work domain expertise in the family; father was a police head constable, but the family's middle-class stability and moral environment shaped Satyarthi's values.
primary_early_advantage_tags: middle-class background, direct exposure to child labor, caste discrimination awareness, engineering education
evidence_summary: Satyarthi was born into a middle-class Brahmin family in Vidisha. His father was a police head constable and his mother an uneducated but morally principled woman. From age five, he was disturbed by the sight of child labor, and at age 11 he collected books for underprivileged children. He dropped his caste surname at 15 after witnessing caste discrimination. He earned engineering degrees and worked as a lecturer before founding Bachpan Bachao Andolan in 1980 at age 26, giving up a lucrative career. His direct childhood exposure to child poverty and caste injustice was the primary catalyst.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, India; father was a retired police head constable, mother a housewife with little formal education but strong moral convictions.
current_position: Nobel Peace Prize laureate (2014); founder of Bachpan Bachao Andolan and multiple child rights organizations; continues activism through the Kailash Satyarthi Children's Foundation and Satyarthi Movement for Global Compassion.

Co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai for their struggle against the suppression of children and for the right to education.
Continues global advocacy through the Satyarthi Movement for Global Compassion and the Kailash Satyarthi Children's Foundation.

name: Mikael Tariverdiev
milestone_by_age_26: Had two one-act ballets staged at the Tbilisi Theater of Opera and Ballet while a student at the Tbilisi musical school around age 19, marking his first professional success as a composer.
early_history_summary: Tariverdiev grew up in a well-off Armenian family in Tbilisi and showed early musical talent, writing his school's anthem. After being forced to finish school in an evening program due to a disciplinary conflict, he attended the Tbilisi musical school for one year, during which he composed two ballets that were staged at the Tbilisi Opera House. He then studied at the Yerevan Conservatory and the Moscow Gnessin Institute under Aram Khachaturian, graduating in 1957.
family_context_summary: Born to a well-off Armenian family in Tbilisi; grandfather Grisho Akopov was a well-known landowner who owned a three-storey brick mansion and a large orchard by the river. Mother Sato dedicated herself entirely to raising Mikael, the only child.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct musical domain expertise in the family, but the family's wealth and social standing in Tbilisi provided access to cultural institutions and music education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: well-off family, Tbilisi Opera House access, Gnessin Institute, Khachaturian mentorship, early musical talent
evidence_summary: Tariverdiev was born into a prosperous Armenian family in Tbilisi with a landowner grandfather. He showed early musical talent by composing his school's anthem. After a disciplinary conflict forced him to finish school in an evening program, he attended the Tbilisi musical school for one year, where he composed two one-act ballets that were staged at the Tbilisi Opera and Ballet Theatre by students of the Choreographic College. He then studied at the Yerevan Conservatory and the Gnessin Institute under Aram Khachaturian. Awarded the title of People's Artist of Russia.

name: Scatman John

He did not release his first album until 1986 and achieved international fame only in 1994-95 with his fusion of scat singing and dance music.

name: Nino Benvenuti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European amateur super-welterweight championship in 1957 at age 19, followed by a second European title in 1959 and Olympic gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics at age 22, receiving the Val Barker Trophy for best boxing style. His father was a fishmonger and boxing enthusiast who trained at the Trieste Boxing Academy. Nino started boxing informally as a child and won the Italian welterweight title in 1956 at age 18, the European title in 1957 at 19, and Olympic gold in 1960 at 22, compiling a 120-0 amateur record before turning professional in 1961.
family_context_summary: Born in Isola d'Istria (now Slovenia) to a working-class Italian family; father Fernando was a fishmonger with a shop in Trieste and a boxing enthusiast. The family fled Istria as refugees after WWII when Nino was 16, losing their home and possessions.

name: Valentin Bondarenko
milestone_by_age_26: Selected on March 7, 1960 at age 23 as one of the first 20 Soviet cosmonauts from 3,000 applicants for the Vostok manned spaceflight program, the youngest member of the inaugural cosmonaut corps.
early_history_summary: Bondarenko was born in Kharkiv, Ukrainian SSR. His father was sent to the Eastern Front in WWII, leaving young Valentin and his mother in wartime hardship. Fascinated by aviation from an early age, he joined an aviation club and graduated from the Armavir Higher Air Force Pilots School in 1957 as a military jet pilot. In 1960, at age 23, he was selected from 3,000 applicants as one of the first 20 Soviet cosmonauts for the Vostok program. He died on March 23, 1961 at age 24 in a fire during a pressure chamber experiment.

name: Jeannette Altwegg
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in ladies' singles figure skating at the 1948 St. Moritz Winter Olympics at age 17, followed by World and European championship titles in 1951 and Olympic gold at the 1952 Oslo Winter Olympics at age 21.
early_history_summary: Altwegg was born in Bombay, India to a Swiss cotton merchant father and Scottish mother. The family moved to Liverpool when she was two. She began skating at age six at the Liverpool Palace Ice Rink and was removed from school at age ten for private tuition to focus on skating and tennis. She was also a junior Wimbledon tennis finalist in 1947. She won the British figure skating title in 1947, Olympic bronze in 1948 at 17, and progressed steadily to win World and European titles in 1951 and Olympic gold in 1952 at 21 before retiring.
family_context_summary: Born in Bombay (now Mumbai), India to a Swiss cotton merchant father working at the Liverpool Cotton Exchange and a Scottish mother. The family moved to Liverpool when Jeannette was two. Her father arranged skating lessons and supported her dual focus on skating and tennis, even removing her from school at age ten for private tuition to accommodate training.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Herman Altwegg worked at the Liverpool Cotton Exchange and was supportive of Jeannette's skating, taking her to the ice rink from age six and arranging lessons with multiple coaches. No direct skating domain expertise in the family, but strong parental investment in her athletic development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Jacques Gerschwiler coaching, Liverpool ice rink, early specialization, parental investment, dual sport talent, compulsory figures expertise
evidence_summary: Altwegg was born in Bombay to a Swiss cotton merchant father and Scottish mother. The family moved to Liverpool when she was two, and her father began taking her to the Liverpool Palace Ice Rink at age six. She was removed from school at age ten for private tuition to focus on skating and tennis. She was coached by Ernst Hartung, Armand Perren, and notably Jacques Gerschwiler, who developed her strong compulsory figures. She won the British title in 1947, Olympic bronze at 17 in 1948, and progressed to World, European, and Olympic gold by 21. Her father's financial support, early specialization, and high-quality coaching were the key advantages.

current_position: Died June 18, 2021 in Switzerland at age 90; final role: retired figure skater who worked with war orphans at Pestalozzi Children's Village after her Olympic victory, later married and raised four children.

Died June 18 in Switzerland; remembered as the last British woman to win Olympic figure skating gold.
